blog_summary: Adrian Colyer discusses a Microsoft internal study examining how software engineering practices are evolving with the rise of AI and ML across the company. The post highlights Microsoft's widespread integration of ML across diverse application areas (e.g., search, healthcare, fraud detection) and the varied expertise levels of teams involved. Colyer emphasizes the shift from specialized data science roles to specialized teams (domain experts, modelers, platform builders) as ML scales. Key insights include the complexity of ML workflows, the critical importance of data management (versioning, quality, accessibility), and the challenges of integrating ML components into traditional software development processes. The study identifies three fundamental differences between ML and traditional software engineering: data management, model customization/reuse, and the entanglement of AI components, which can lead to non-monotonic error propagation in large systems.
